name: Helms Cable Row
description: The Helms cable row (a variation associated with physique coach Eric Helms) positions the lifter on a high-incline bench facing a low cable pulley, with the torso supported at approximately 60-70 degrees. This angle creates a combined vertical and horizontal pull that maximally stretches the lats and teres major throughout the range of motion, and the chest support eliminates lower back involvement.

execution.starting_position: Set a bench at 60-70 degrees incline near a low cable pulley. Lie prone with chest on the pad, feet on the floor. Grab the cable handle (rope, V-handle, or bar) with arms extended toward the pulley.
execution.setup_instructions: Position the bench close enough to the cable stack that the arms are fully extended toward the pulley in the starting position.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms fully extended, feeling a deep lat stretch.
Step 2: Row the cable toward the torso, driving elbows back.
Step 3: At peak contraction, hold 1 second.
Step 4: Return under control to full arm extension.
Step 5: Emphasize the stretch at the bottom — this differentiates the Helms row.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale returning to the stretch.
common_mistakes: Bench angle too low — the incline must be steep enough to allow full lat stretch
Insufficient cable distance — the bench must be positioned to achieve true full extension
safety_considerations: Adjust cable height and bench position carefully before loading
Keep the neck neutral — avoid craning while lying prone
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximum lat stretch at full arm extension to full retraction at peak contraction.
coaching_cues: Let the weight pull you into a full stretch at the bottom
The bench angle is what makes this special — get it right
